messages:
maya: FYI I just noticed a regression in the long-context replay run after the kernel_picker tune earlier today. p99 latency up ~18% on prefill-heavy traces.
aj: Oof. Which run/commit? can you paste the harness command and the perf summary?
maya: Run: `./harness/run_replay --trace=2026-03-longmix-prefill.json --kernel-selector=v2 --batch-policy=dynamic --warm-kv=true`
maya: Summary (replay node): tokens/sec 21.3 -> 20.2, p50 42ms -> 45ms, p95 120ms -> 138ms, p99 210ms -> 248ms. GPU util looks steady tho.
perf-bot: perf/regression detected: tag=kernel-selector-v2, metric=p99_latency, delta=+18%, baseline=kernel-selector-v1
sandeep: Do we see different kernels chosen during the prefill vs decode phases? last time the selector used avg_seq_len and mispredicted for long-prefill mixes.
carla: Quick check: synthetic longmix (fixed seqlen=4k for warmup + 512 decode) vs replay (many short + occasional long). They exercise kernel switch paths differently.
maya: I pulled the kernel logs. snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:10Z] request=abc kernel=kv-opt-v1 seq=4096 phase=prefill
[2026-03-18T09:12:10Z] request=abc kernel=attn-fused-v2 seq=512 phase=decode
[2026-03-18T09:12:11Z] request=def kernel=attn-fused-v1 seq=1024 phase=prefill
[2026-03-18T09:12:11Z] request=def kernel=attn-fused-v2 seq=64 phase=decode
```
maya: v2 selector is picking attn-fused-v2 for many mid-long prefill windows but it has worse single-token latency for some seqlen/batch combos.
aj: Can we repro with pinned kernels? run both with `--force-kernel=attn-fused-v1` and `--force-kernel=attn-fused-v2` and compare.
sandeep: Also run microbench per-kernel with the exact seq/batch distribution from the replay. I suspect the selector's cost model underweights prefill amortization.
carla: Note: replay harness includes prefix caching in a way synthetic does not. For prefill-heavy workloads, the KV-cache population time is nontrivial and affects which kernel gives best end-to-end p99.
nate: I ran a quick microbench on A10g yesterday. For seq=4096 batch=1 attn-fused-v2 was 6% slower p99 than v1, but v2 has better throughput at batch>=4. Selector probably over-optimizing throughput.
maya: Proposed experiment plan (short):
- reproduce regression on same commit with `--trace` and save full kernel logs
- run 3 controlled experiments: (1) replay baseline, (2) replay with forced-kernel v1, (3) replay with forced-kernel v2
- run microbench per-kernel with exact seq/batch histogram from the trace
- nvprof capture for one representative request with prefill
- compare p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec + GPU mem/KV cache hit ratio
carla: Also add an apples->controlled comparison: normalize batch sizes, set `--max-batch=8` and `--batch-window=5ms` so both runs use the same batching envelope.
aj: prefer the term "controlled comparisons" over apples-to-apples in doc :slightly_smiling_face:
sandeep: I'll own the microbench script (`tools/perf/microbench_from_hist.py`) and run it across kernel builds. ETA EOD.
maya: I'll collect the full replay trace and annotate the seq-length histogram and per-request phase durations.
nate: I'll generate nvprof and topo logs, and sanity-check CUDA kernels called. ping me when trace uploaded.
perf-bot: checklist created: /perf/issues/3248 - reproduce and isolate kernel-selector regressing on prefill-heavy longmix
maya: One more note: in the selector code the cost model uses expected tokens-per-window but we saw heavy skew: 10% of requests are prefill-dominant and drive p99. We should include tail-weighted objective when scoring kernels.
carla: Good call. For methodology doc: recommend including these items for long-context benchmarks: 1) explicit prefill vs decode phase labels, 2) seq-length histograms, 3) forced-kernel runs, 4) batching envelope normalization, 5) KV warm/cold toggles.
aj: OK. Next steps: sandeep + nate + maya run the experiments today, carla will draft a short methodology note we can add to `docs/perf/benchmarking.md`.
maya: Thanks. If someone can kick off the forced-kernel runs on the replay infra that'd help — I don't have access to that pool.
carla: I'll start a run and post the run id here when live.
maya: :thumbsup:
